chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.

From Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him), He breathed into him from the Spirit, so there was in him a breath from Allah, the Exalted. Then He said to him: Go to the sky and build for Me a house. Adam went and built the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Then he returned to Allah, the Exalted, and He said: O Adam, have you seen what you built? He said: Yes. He said: Then it is your house that you will enter. Adam entered the house, and there was in it a breath from Allah, the Exalted. When Allah, the Exalted, created Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) from the breath of Adam, He placed in him a breath from Allah, the Exalted. He is the Imam after him, for he is the Imam who guides to the truth and knows the truth, for he is the Imam who guides to the truth and knows the truth, for he is the Imam who guides to the truth and knows the truth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual connection between Adam, Prophet Muhammad, and the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to substantiate the doctrine of *Nur Muhammad* (the Light of Muhammad), illustrating the continuous spiritual chain (*silsila*) of Imamate from Adam through to the Twelve Imams. This establishes the Imams not merely as political successors but as the primordial locus of divine guidance, reinforcing their infallibility (*Ismah*) and unique ontological status in Shia theology.
